rossmore-forest-park: A former Rossmore estate with trails, wooden sculptures, lakes and the ruins of old gateways.
castle-leslie-estate: A Leslie family estate since 1660, with a Victorian castle, an equestrian centre, a lake and trails.
belturbet-railway-station: A restored narrow-gauge railway station, with a railway museum and period carriages.
cavan-county-museum: An award-winning museum with Ireland's largest outdoor First World War trench replica.
shannon-pot: The source of the River Shannon, Ireland's longest river, in a karst pool on the slopes of Cuilcagh.
dun-a-ri-forest-park: A forest park with ice houses, a Roman bridge and local legends, on the banks of the River Cabra.
killykeen-forest-park: Wooded peninsulas among the islands of Lough Oughter, with trails, kayaking and fishing.
cavan-burren-park: A karst landscape with megaliths, dolmens and interpretive trails in the Marble Arch Caves Global Geopark.
sean-mac-diarmada-cottage: The birthplace of one of the signatories of the 1916 Proclamation, preserved as a museum in north Leitrim.
lough-rynn-castle-gardens: Historic gardens of the Clements estate, with a maze, a walled garden and views over the lake.
lough-allen: A jagged lake on the upper Shannon, ringed by the Arigna and Sliabh an Iarainn mountains.
acres-lake-floating-boardwalk: A 600 m floating boardwalk over Lough Allen, part of the Shannon Blueway, with trails and kayaking.
parkes-castle: A restored 17th-century fortified castle on the shores of Lough Gill, with an exhibition about the plantation.
glencar-waterfall: A 15-metre waterfall immortalised by W.B. Yeats, near Sligo, with a short trail and a picnic area.
roscommon-castle: A 13th-century Norman castle in evocative ruins, surrounded by a public park and lake.
lough-key-forest-park: A forest park with islands, an observation tower, a zip line, bungalows and trails for all ages.
arigna-mining-experience: A guided tour of a real coal mine led by former miners, in the Arigna hills.
strokestown-park-famine-museum: A Georgian mansion with the National Famine Museum and restored walled gardens.
boyle-abbey: A 12th-century Cistercian abbey with an impressive cloister, in the heart of Boyle.
rathcroghan: The ancient royal capital of Connacht and gateway to the Otherworld in Irish mythology.
lough-ree: A great lake on the River Shannon with islands, fishing, boat trips and riverside beaches.
newcastle-wood: A forest of conifers and broadleaves with peaceful trails near Ballymahon.
royal-canal-greenway: A 130 km greenway along the Royal Canal, from Dublin to Cloondara — the final stretch is in Longford.
granard-motte-bailey: A 12th-century Norman motte on an ancient hill, with a St Kitirine statue and wide views.
ardagh-heritage-village: An award-winning heritage village, with a picturesque village green and an interpretive centre.
